channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: British Pound surges against US Dollar ahead of US NFP data
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) trades 0.5% higher to near 1.3340 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday.

item.title: US Dollar: Labor focus softens – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that the US Nonfarm Payrolls release is unlikely to have the market impact it once did, even as recent JOLTS data point to improving hiring and fewer layoffs.

item.title: Euro weakens vs British Pound as softer Eurozone inflation, divided ECB weigh
item.description: EUR/GBP trades around 0.8550 on Thursday, down 0.21% on the day, as the Euro (EUR) remains under pressure against the British Pound (GBP) after another batch of data reinforced expectations of a more cautious European Central Bank (ECB).

item.title: US Nonfarm Payrolls set to grow above 100K for fourth straight month, signaling labor market resilience
item.description: The United States (US) Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) will release the Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for June on Thursday at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Dollar finds support at previous resistance area around 161.00
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) staged a sharp rebound against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, raising speculation about potential action by the Japanese Ministry of Finance (MoF).

item.title: Indian Rupee: State-bank selling caps gains – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale highlights that state-controlled banks in India have been actively selling Dollars for a second day after USD/INR briefly moved above its 50-day moving average.

item.title: CEE FX: Mixed PMI and inflation keep zloty capped – ING
item.description: Frantisek Taborsky at ING notes diverging PMI signals in Central Europe, with strong Czech sentiment and weaker Poland, but still expects Polish growth above 3% in 2026. Softer Polish inflation and a potentially dovish National Bank of Poland outlook are reflected in modest rate-cut pricing.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $59.92 per troy ounce, up 1.38% from the $59.10 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Upside potential builds – UOB
item.description: UOB strategist Quek Ser Leang highlights a constructive technical backdrop for the US Dollar Index (DXY), noting similarities with the 2021 and 2025 basing phases.

item.title: RBNZ: Policy pace and July hike – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Prashant Newnaha expects the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) to raise the Official Cash Rate (OCR) by 25bps to 2.50% at next week’s meeting, keeping policy too accommodative with the cash rate still below neutral.

item.title: Japan’s Finance Ministry declines to comment on the Yen's sudden spike
item.description: When asked about the sudden spike in the Japanese Yen (JPY), Japan’s Finance Ministry declined to comment, per Reuters.

item.title: Euro remains stronger against Canadian Dollar following Eurozone Unemployment Rate
item.description: EUR/CAD rises after two days of losses, trading around 1.6200 during the European hours on Thursday. The pair remains stronger as the Euro (EUR) holds ground following the release of the Eurozone Unemployment Rate, which came in at 6.2% in May, against the 6.3% expected.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Inflation signals strengthen – Commerzbank
item.description: Volkmar Baur at Commerzbank highlights solid Japanese activity data, with the manufacturing PMI at 54.8 and the Tankan business conditions index at its highest since 2003.

item.title: British Pound: Sterling gains strength against Euro – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists highlight that EUR/GBP has completed a Head and Shoulders pattern and broken below its neckline around 0.8610, now seen as initial resistance.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Consolidates below $68.00, lowest since February amid oversold RSI
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – enters a bearish consolidation phase near its lowest level since late February, set earlier this Friday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar rises as US Dollar holds losses ahead of US NFP data
item.description: USD/CAD has lost its recent gains from the previous day, trading around 1.4190 during the European hours on Thursday. Traders adopt a cautious stance ahead of the highly anticipated June Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report.

item.title: Euro: Fed story caps upside against US Dollar – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING highlights softer Eurozone inflation and questions over a September ECB hike, with 15bp still priced but subsidies expiry possibly lifting prices later.

item.title: Australian Dollar licks its wounds around 0.6900 awaiting US Nonfarm Payrolls data
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) remains practically flat against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, consolidating losses after having depreciated nearly 4% in June. The AUD/USD pair is trading within a broadly 65-pip range, with downside attempts contained at 0.6865 and bulls limited below 0.6930 so far.

item.title: Indian Rupee falls back despite multiple tailwinds
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) surrenders early gains and turns marginally lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises to near $59.60 as US Dollar slumps ahead of US NFP data
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades 0.9% higher to near $59.65 during the European trading session on Thursday. The white metal gains as the US Dollar (USD) slumps ahead of the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for June, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Brent: Dovish momentum with geopolitical support – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Early Morning Reid, authored by Henry Allen and colleagues, highlights a sharp decline in Brent Oil as geopolitical developments ease inflation concerns. Brent crude has fallen to a four‑month low near $71.57/bbl and extended losses toward $70.81/bbl.

item.title: Gold clings to intraday gains as USD remains on the back foot ahead of US NFP
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its bid tone through the first half of the European session on Thursday amid a modest US Dollar (USD) downtick, though it lacks follow-through and remains confined within the previous day's broader range.

item.title: US Dollar: NFP risk to extend gains – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes Fed Chair Warsh struck a less hawkish tone, with inflation expectations and risks having come down, and policy assumptions now based on no further Fed hikes.

item.title: Dow Jones futures edge lower ahead of US Nonfarm Payrolls
item.description: The Dow Jones futures decline 0.15% to trade near 52,600, while S&P 500 futures fall 0.24%, trading near 7,520. Meanwhile, Nasdaq 100 futures lose 0.80% to trade near 29,850 during European trading hours on Thursday.

item.title: Euro climbs further beyond 1.1400 as USD weakens ahead of US NFP report
item.description: The EUR/USD pair builds on its intraday ascent and reclaims the 1.1400 mark during the early part of the European session on Thursday, reversing a major part of the overnight losses to the weekly low.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Softer PMI supports RBI hold – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts note India’s final June manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) was revised down to 54.2, marking the second-slowest expansion in four years, with broad moderation across output, orders and employment.

item.description: Here is what you need to know on Thursday, July 2:

item.title: What is keeping the British Pound tied to fiscal risks as the BoE looks set to keep rates steady?
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) remains tightly bound to the UK’s evolving inflation outlook and impending fiscal policy choices.

item.title: Euro tumbles against Japanese Yen on suspected Japan’s intervention
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is down almost 0.5% to near 184.00 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) during the European trading session on Thursday. The EUR/JPY pair slumps as the Japanese Yen (JPY) delivers a sudden strong upside move, which appears to be the outcome of Japan’s intervention.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Neutral within broader downtrend against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes AUD/USD has slipped into a tight consolidation after a strong rebound to 0.6930, trading between 0.6883 and 0.6921 and closing at 0.6894. He expects intraday range trading between 0.6880 and 0.6915.
